  "summary": "S1 — Fact: deliver a Python CLI that reads sales CSVs and prints total revenue, revenue by region, and units by product. S2 — Fact: add tests. Boundary facts: this stage is intake only, the repository is empty, and this exercise provides no tools or files; no implementation is performed. Assumption: the consumer is a local shell user, the entry point accepts CSV paths, and the deliverable is source and tests usable in a local Python environment. The named CLI target authorizes delivery there; no deployed target is requested. In an isolated run, the source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, when the result becomes visible; a deployed outcome would exist only after release. Interaction and state defaults: there is no interactive session or shared application state; the operating system identifies the invoking user, local file permissions govern visibility, aggregates live in process memory until exit, and a restart recomputes them. Concurrent input changes have unspecified results; discovery should establish any runtime guarantees before relying on them. Open questions, all assigned to discovery with recorded defaults if evidence is absent: (1) Establish representative sales files and any authoritative schema first; this blocks field names, valid values, revenue calculation, multi-file behavior, and expected totals. Default to UTF-8 CSVs with region, product, quantity, and unit_price headers, revenue as quantity multiplied by unit_price, and aggregation across supplied files. (2) Establish consumer conventions and examples first; this blocks the command name, exact arguments, output formatting, and error wording. Default to positional file paths, human-readable text, exit zero on success, and nonzero with an error on failure. (3) Establish the execution environment and any project conventions first; this blocks Python version selection and final test command. Default to an available Python 3 runtime, standard-library dependencies, and unittest discovery. (4) Establish whether input files can change during a run and what the runtime provides first; this blocks any stronger concurrency or visibility guarantees. Default to ordinary local filesystem permissions and no concurrency guarantee. Discovery source hints are unverified leads: representative CSVs, workspace or team conventions, relevant channels and internal documentation, private repositories, and an owner able to explain sales fields and revenue; none is identified in the request. Treat ambiguous terms such as sales record, revenue, and units as leads. Store any sensitive locator only in an authorized private store, never in committed KNOWLEDGE/. The principal risk is choosing a schema or calculation that differs from the intended data."
